title: Father's Tuskegee education and black colleges in Louisiana
summary: Lee says his father graduated from Tuskegee and relates how Grambling was founded with Booker T. Washington's help.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: He studied where? At the Tuskegee Institute or something like that?
Yes, he did. He graduated from Tuskegee Institute.
I have no idea. I told you about those years! I have no idea.
Well, was it unusual for there to be black professors in 19 -- what? In the teens in Louisiana?
Oh, I don't really think so. I think ...

I don't really know, but I was thinking, I don't really think so because, like, I was reading the Times this morning and on the Sports page they were talking about Grambling University -- you know, that's quite a football force, in the black colleges.
And I read an article where they said how Grambling came about was that -- it was a white man's name, and a couple

of black people got together and called Booker T. Washington and they corresponded with one another then, who was at Tuskegee, and told them that they wanted to start a college there in Louisiana called Grambling College, and Booker T. sent someone down from Tuskegee, so now they said -- this seems like it was 1908 -- so you know, I don't know if he sent the Professor down then, so they must have had something to ...
New Orleans University was a black university?
Yeah. New Orleans University I think is now Southern University.
